wa.hero.badge: HINAWI WRITING ACADEMY • Professional Writing & Correspondence Studio
wa.hero.title: Academy of Writing and Formal Correspondence
wa.hero.sub: Learn to write clear, persuasive and respectful emails, master cover letters, and avoid the common mistakes that slip into most drafts.
wa.tpl.formal_email.title: Formal Business Email
wa.tpl.formal_email.rule1: Always open with a formal salutation such as Dear Mr. / Ms. followed by the family name.
wa.tpl.formal_email.rule2: Pick the connector that expresses the right relationship; "and" and "but" also work when needed.
wa.tpl.formal_email.rule3: Use the future perfect to stress deadline commitment: "will have deployed".
wa.tpl.job_application.title: Job Application Cover Letter
wa.tpl.job_application.rule1: Name the position clearly in the first line.
wa.tpl.job_application.rule2: Tie your past achievements to the company's future goals.
wa.tpl.job_application.rule3: Close with a professional sign-off such as Sincerely or Respectfully.
wa.tpl.essay.title: Academic Opinion Essay
wa.tpl.essay.rule1: Open with a strong hook and topic sentence.
wa.tpl.essay.rule2: Support your opinion with real statistics and evidence.
wa.tpl.essay.rule3: Avoid slang like "cool, stuff, a lot of".
wa.tpl.complaint.title: Formal Complaint Letter
wa.tpl.complaint.rule1: Keep a calm formal tone without anger or excess emotion.
wa.tpl.complaint.rule2: Pin down the problem with numbers and dates: order number, delivery date.
wa.tpl.complaint.rule3: Use the future perfect for your time expectations: "will have investigated".
wa.tpl.university.title: University Application Essay
wa.tpl.university.rule1: Open with a short personal story linking your passion to the field.
wa.tpl.university.rule2: Cite concrete achievements with numbers: projects, volunteer hours.
wa.tpl.university.rule3: Link your past to your future with the future perfect: "will have completed".

wa.feedback.error: Could not reach the analysis service. Your draft is still here. No automated assessment is available right now; use the self-review checklist in the workshops above.
wa.mistakes.title: Most Common Writing Mistakes
wa.mistakes.sub: Avoid these three slips that drag down your score in academic and professional writing:
wa.mistake1.title: Joining independent clauses without proper punctuation (Run-on Sentences)
wa.mistake1.explanation: Do not join two complete sentences without a time connector or proper comma.
wa.mistake2.title: The subject-verb agreement trap
wa.mistake2.explanation: "Every" is always singular, so it takes "has", not "have".
wa.mistake3.title: The trap of using "will" after time connectors
wa.mistake3.explanation: After "By the time" we use the present simple (arrive) for future meaning.

sp.rec.note: Local recording up to 90 seconds for self-review. It is not sent to any server and is not an automated pronunciation score. The recording is deleted when you close the practice.
sp.rec.live: Microphone is on. Press stop when you finish.
sp.step1.note: Original educational dialogue. The audio button uses the available reading voice, not a native-speaker recording.
sp.step3.hintA: Still needs fixing. Hint: the word starts with the letter
sp.step3.hintC: letters. Review the dialogue and try again.
sp.step4.note: Tap the words in order. Each word has its own slot even if it repeats.
sp.step4.correct: Excellent. The phrase order is correct.
sp.step4.retry: The order is still off. Listen to speaker B's line and try again.
sp.step5.note: Answer with your voice or practice out loud. Listen to yourself and tick what you did. This is self-review, not a pronunciation score.
sp.check1: I answered the question with a full reply that fits the situation.
sp.check2: I added a personal detail or reason instead of only memorizing the model.
sp.check3: I listened to myself or repeated the reply and checked its clarity.
sp.complete.hint: Solve the 3 activities correctly and finish your self-review to save the lesson. Repeating the lesson does not add XP again.
